claims.text: Most research to date on digital technology usage and adolescent mental health has been correlational.
Most research to date on digital technology usage has focused on adults rather than adolescents.
Research on digital technology usage and adolescent mental health has generated a mix of conflicting small positive, negative, and null associations.
Recent large-scale preregistered studies report small associations between daily digital technology usage and adolescents' well-being.
Associations reported in recent large-scale preregistered studies do not offer a way of distinguishing cause from effect.
The estimated associations between daily digital technology usage and adolescents' well-being are unlikely to be of clinical or practical significance.

evidence.description: The review highlights that most research to date has been correlational.
The review highlights that most research to date has been focused on adults versus adolescents.
The review notes that research has generated a mix of often conflicting small positive, negative and null associations.
The most recent and rigorous large-scale preregistered studies report small associations between the amount of daily digital technology usage and adolescents' well-being.
Large-scale preregistered studies report associations that do not offer a way of distinguishing cause from effect.
Estimated associations between daily digital technology usage and well-being, as estimated, are unlikely to be of clinical or practical significance.

methodologies.name: Literature Review Synthesis
methodologies.description: Synthesized data from narrative reviews, meta-analyses, large-scale preregistered cohort studies, and intensive longitudinal and ecological momentary assessment studies.
datasets: intensive longitudinal and ecological momentary assessment studies

limitations.text: Most research to date has been correlational and does not offer a way of distinguishing cause from effect.
Most prior research focused on adults versus adolescents.
Prior research has generated a mix of often conflicting small positive, negative, and null associations.

future_work.text: Improve future research methodologies regarding adolescent digital technology usage and mental health.
Develop strategies and frameworks for supporting adolescents' mental health in the digital age.
